pr_title: src,lib: print source map error source on demand
pr_body:
The source context is not prepended to the value of the `stack` property when the source map is not enabled. Rather than prepending the error source context to the value of the `stack` property unconditionally,  this PR aligns the behavior and only prints the source context when the error is not handled by userland (e.g. fatal errors).

Also, this PR fixes that when source-map support is enabled, the error source context is not pointing to where the error was thrown. For a source file "test.js" like:
```js
const err = new Error('foo');
throw err;
```

The source context for the thrown error should be:
```
test.js:2
throw err; // << where the error was thrown
^

Error: foo
    at test.js:1:13 // << where the error was created
```

Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/43186
Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/41541
pr_comments: @bcoe thank you for the suggestion! Updated with stricter nullish check. :)
@nodejs/cpp-reviewers would be good to have someone take a look at this PR.

@legendecas I'd make the case that, even though you could squint and call this a breaking change, perhaps it's worth landing in a patch, when we weigh the performance benefits against the likeliness of breaking people:

- If it breaks people, it's most likely to break test suites.
- The benefit of performance improvements for people printing errors might outweigh the cost of breakages for others.

This might be a question worth bringing to @nodejs/tsc
@nodejs/tsc would you be willing to land this in Node v18 with do-not-backport flags for v16?

Updated with a benchmark on accessing the `error.stack` property and the improvement in my local environment is considerable:

```
                                                      confidence improvement accuracy (*)   (**)  (***)
es/error-stack.js n=100000 method='sourcemap'                ***     59.82 %       ±1.97% ±2.65% ±3.50%
es/error-stack.js n=100000 method='without-sourcemap'                 0.07 %       ±0.58% ±0.77% ±1.01%
```

Benchmark CI: https://ci.nodejs.org/view/Node.js%20benchmark/job/benchmark-node-micro-benchmarks/1170/

```
                                                      confidence improvement accuracy (*)   (**)  (***)
es/error-stack.js n=100000 method='sourcemap'                ***     51.74 %       ±4.54% ±6.04% ±7.87%
es/error-stack.js n=100000 method='without-sourcemap'                 0.68 %       ±2.05% ±2.74% ±3.57%
```

We never handled the way we printed errors as breaking changes as it relies upon so many things.
We just recently added the AggregationError's `errors` property to be displayed by default as a patch or minor change and similar with the `cause` property. We also changed the way we print the stack by adding more colors as patch or minor.
As such, I would also not count this as breaking.
We just discussed this in the TSC meeting and no one objected against removing the label. As such, there's no reason not to backport this anymore.
This can either be handled as patch or minor. I suggest @legendecas you decide upon that as you originally added the label?
Thank you for the suggestion! I believe a semver-minor is more appropriate as it is changing the `error.stack` format so I'm landing this as a semver-minor one.
@mcollina any specific reason why it should not be backported to e.g., v16?
Possible breakages. Maybe we could just label it as "backing" and reevaluate in a few months.

issue_context.title: `--enable-source-maps` adds error context before stack string
issue_context.body:
### Version

v18.2.0

### Platform

Darwin mbp.local 21.5.0 Darwin Kernel Version 21.5.0: Tue Apr 26 21:08:29 PDT 2022; root:xnu-8020.121.3~4/RELEASE_ARM64_T8101 arm64

### Subsystem

_No response_

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

When accessing `Error.stack` without source maps, only the error string and error frames are produced. However, when using `--enable-source-maps`, the context of the original error is prefixed to this output. I don't think this expected behavior (see below for why).

To reproduce, compile the following TypeScript program with `tsc --sourceMap true`:

```typescript
function main() {
  try {
    throw new Error('Message');
  } catch (err: any) {
    console.error(err.stack);
  }
}

main();
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

You need to use the `--enable-source-maps` command line flag when running Node.

### What is the expected behavior?

When turning on source maps, I only expect the symbols and filenames to be rewritten:

```shell
$ node --enable-source-maps build/app.js
Error: Message
    at main (/app.ts:3:11)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/app.ts:9:1)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1105:14)
    at Module._extensions..js (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1159:10)
    at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:981:32)
    at Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:827:12)
    at Function.executeUserEntryPoint [as runMain] (node:internal/modules/run_main:77:12)
    at node:internal/main/run_main_module:17:47
```

I don't expect that turning on source maps would do anything but rewrite the symbols and filenames using source maps. While this may be helpful, it significantly changes the output of `Error.stack`, in a way that is not compatible with the TC39 proposal for error stacks, nor with standard V8 output that tools rely on.

Including an "error context" is not part of the [Stage 1 Error Stacks proposal](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-error-stacks), where [the specification for the `GetStackString` operation specifies how to construct the "stack string"](https://tc39.es/proposal-error-stacks/#sec-getstackstring):

> ## 3 GetStackString ( error )
> When the abstract operation `GetStackString` is called with argument `error`, the following steps are performed:
> [...]
> 6. Let `stackString` be the concatenation of `errorString`, the code unit 0x000A (LINE FEED), and `frameString`.

This can also break systems that rely on errors being reported exactly as returned by V8. For example, Google Cloud Error Reporting requires that you log errors exactly as returned by V8 in order for them to get picked up. See also:

* https://cloud.google.com/error-reporting/docs/formatting-error-messages#formatting_requirements
* https://cloud.google.com/error-reporting/reference/rest/v1beta1/projects.events/report#ReportedErrorEvent

### What do you see instead?

The output includes an "error context" prefixed to the stack, that looks like this:

```shell
$ node --enable-source-maps build/app.js
/app.ts:3
    throw new Error('Message');
          ^

Error: Message
    at main (/app.ts:3:11)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/app.ts:9:1)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1105:14)
    at Module._extensions..js (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1159:10)
    at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:981:32)
    at Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:827:12)
    at Function.executeUserEntryPoint [as runMain] (node:internal/modules/run_main:77:12)
    at node:internal/main/run_main_module:17:47
```


### Additional information

https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/37252 would change how `--enable-source-maps` output is formatted, with the purpose of aligning with the [Error Stacks proposal](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-error-stacks). However, this PR retains the printing of an error context above the "actual" stack (formatted according to the proposal). It therefore seems to be a goal to follow the spec—but I think including context violates the spec.

Printing the original exception context was introduced in https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/33491. This PR references that before this change, the transpiled source would be displayed. I'm not sure exactly what the format was back then, or if any context was printed.
comments:
To be fair the error stack proposal is _very_ early stage and may change and I would caution aligning to it and Node is the platform so expecting Node to align its core features to google cloud error reporting seems a bit backwards.

That said: I can see a consistency argument here and I'm wondering what users would find better.

cc @bcoe

The reason "error context" is added, was an effort to align behavior close with Node.js' treatment of errors when `--enable-source-maps` is not enabled:

```js
const foo = () => {
  throw Error('beep boop');
}
foo()
```

```bash
$ node foo.js 
/Users/benjamincoe/foo.js:2
  throw Error('beep boop');
  ^

Error: beep boop
    at foo (/Users/benjamincoe/foo.js:2:9)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/Users/benjamincoe/foo.js:4:1)
    at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1085:14)
    at Object.Module._extensions..js (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1114:10)
    at Module.load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:950:32)
    at Function.Module._load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:790:12)
    at Function.executeUserEntryPoint [as runMain] (internal/modules/run_main.js:76:12)
    at internal/main/run_main_module.js:17:47
Benjamins-MacBook-Pro:~ benjamincoe$ 
```

The decision to include the additional context has been a bit of a nuisance, one issue being it hurts performance.

I'd be supportive of dropping the "error context" aligning more closely with the specification. However, I think this would need to be considered a breaking change.
Just for context: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/41541#issuecomment-1183357167. And I'm working on this. :)

review_comments: Is this additional work from your adding support for source maps in evaled code?  `sourceURL=` specifically applies to this right?

No, it's not needed for mapping the stack lines. This is needed to cache the source URL for [GetSourceMapErrorSource](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/43875/files#diff-090d65062da5652b79f8a641489e4bd33b37faf28b8e91cc2ac31ab43084a3d2R60) as explained in the inline comments.
Gotcha, so v8 itself consumes the magic URL and `message->GetScriptResourceName();` will return the URL in the comment 👍
